departure date. 
19.3. Students who have vacated the bedroom but still holding the room key and/or smartcard

without prior notification. Jockey Club Student Village III is not responsible for the loss 
or damage of such items. 
20.4. Residents are responsible for checking and clearing their pigeon hole for any 
correspondence left before withdrawal.

 21.1. Noise level in the vicinity of the Student Village should be kept reasonable at all times and 
be lowered after nightfall.

suspension of residency. Residents should always use Smithfield Road to travel to and 
from the Student Village.

text:
Shun Hing College General Floor Rules
 
 
 
Welcome to Shun Hing College!
 
 
For everyone’s comfort and safety, we ask you to read and observe
 
 
the following rules and guidelines.
 
 
 
Smoking and drinking are prohibited in all areas of the college, including
 
 
student rooms and the immediate areas outside the college.
 
 
The 
​
NO-SMOKING-NO-ALCOHOL
​
 policy is strictly enforced.
 
See College regulations for details.
 
 
Please observe 
​
QUIET HOURS
​
 from 11 pm to 8 am.
 
All non-resident visitors must leave the College by 10:30 pm.
 
Violations could lead to immediate suspension of residency at the College.
 
 
NEVER EVER
​
 leave your food on the stove unattended
 
Intense heat will trigger the fire alarm, alert the Fire Department, and lead to
 
 
building evacuation.
 
 
 
 
1.
Student Lounge (pantry)
 
1.1.
Cabinets
 
1.1.1.
All cabinets are free to use by residents of the floor.
 
1.1.2.
Be 
​
hygienic 
​
and wash all items before storage.
 
 
1.1.3.
Be 
​
fair 
​
and do not take up excessive space.
 
1.1.4.
Be 
​
civil 
​
and do not use or remove items that are not yours.
 
1.1.5.
Be 
​
cautious 
​
and do not store items that you absolutely cannot lose.
 
1.2.
Refrigerator
 
1.2.1.
Do not take up too much refrigerator space.
 
1.2.2.
Store only items that require refrigeration.
 
1.2.3.
Wrap your food appropriately before storing it in the fridge, and
 
remember its expiration date. Put your name, room number, and the
 
date the food was stored on the wrapping or the container.
 
 
1.2.4.
Be 
​
respectful
​
: do not remove food items that don’t belong to you.
 
1.2.5.
Fresh food items should not be refrigerated for more than a week.
 
College staff, floor coordinators, or tutors will remove expired items
 
without prior notice.
 
 

1.3.
Waste and garbage
 
1.3.1.
Put organic and non-recyclable wastes in the lounge bin, or in the
 
dumpster outside the 4/F lobby if the lounge bin is full.
 
 
1.3.2.
Do not litter in the corridor Do not put food waste in the bathroom bins.
 
 
1.3.3.
Recycle 
​
as much as possible. Recycling bins are available on your
 
floor or in the 4/F lift lobby.
 
1.3.4.
Keep all common areas clean and tidy, including the tables, chairs,
 
and the floors. Brooms, towels, mops, and extra bin bags are available
 
in the lounge and washrooms.
 
 
1.4.
Cooking utensils
 
1.4.1.
Clean all utensils immediately after use and stow them away
 
accordingly.
 
1.5.
Electric stoves, microwave oven, and the sink
 
1.5.1.
Turn off the electric stoves, microwave oven, and the main switches
 
on the wall after use.
 
1.5.2.
Keep these appliances clean and always clean them after use.
 
1.5.3.
Never leave behind food scraps.
 
1.6.
Lighting and television
 
1.6.1.
Turn off the lights and the TV if you are the last person to leave the
 
lounge/pantry.
 
1.7.
Air conditioner
 
1.7.1.
Close all windows when the AC is in use.
 
1.7.2.
Turn off the ACs when you are the last person to leave the pantry.
 
1.8.
Whiteboard
 
 
1.8.1.
Use only whiteboard markers. Never use oil-based markers. Always
 
check your marker type before writing.
 
2.
Washroom
 
 
2.1.
Flush the toilet and wash your hands thoroughly each time after use.
 
 
2.2.
Dispose of all hygiene related products carefully.
 
 
2.3.
Do not use the bathroom on an opposite gender floor
​
.
 
2.4.
Place all personal items inside your personal cabinet.
 
2.5.
Always clean the basin and remove the water around the basin after use.
 
2.6.
Do not use the hand-dryer between 11 pm and 8 am.
 
 
3.
Bedroom and corridor
 
3.1.
Keep your room clean. Be considerate to your roommate.
 
 
3.2.
Close doors gently to minimize the noise and nuisance to others.
 
3.3.
Candles, incense, and other open flames are not allowed in the bedroom as
 
they will set off the fire alarm.
 
3.4.
Do not place any personal items in the lounge or in the corridors.
 
3.5.
Personal items left in public areas will be removed without prior notice.
 
 
3.6.
No voice call or loud chats in the corridors between 11 pm and 8 am.
 
3.7.
Finally, when you check out, make sure you clean your room and restore it to
 
its original condition.

he voting/selection process for the FRs is outlined below:

title: Health and Wellness Team
text:
Health and Wellness Team
Trained and reliable first aid
The SHC Health & Wellness Team is dedicated to addressing the growing need for comprehensive care in physical health, mental health, and social well-being within our community. Our mission is to raise awareness of various health issues and promote healthy living practices. We also provide immediate medical assistance for emergency situations in JCSVIII and offer support to those in need.
Our team comprises motivated medical, dental, and nursing students, doctors, healthcare researchers, and students with a passion for Health and Wellness events. We warmly welcome individuals who hold First Aid or Mental Health First Aid qualifications.
What sets us apart:
Mental Health Focus
: Mental health is a significant concern for both our team and society as a whole. We prioritize the mental well-being of our residents and the Kennedy Town community. By organizing relaxation workshops, community bonding projects, sharing talks, and mental illness screening programs, we aim to promote psychological well-being and combat the stigmatization of mental illnesses.
Community Engagement
: We believe in actively engaging with our community. Each year, we organize multiple blood donation drives, health promotion initiatives, and health check-ups in the village and throughout Hong Kong. By giving back to society and sharing our knowledge, we aim to foster understanding between citizens and students. Through these projects, our team members become more passionate and empathetic, creating a positive impact for the future.
Empowerment and Advocacy
: In collaboration with other sports and working teams within the college, we organize a variety of activities to strengthen the bonds among residents and promote healthy lifestyles. Our initiatives aim to empower individuals to take responsibility for their own well-being and the well-being of others, both physically and mentally.
We firmly believe in the power of unity and community. If you share our passion and are interested in our cause, we encourage you to join us or collaborate with us. Together, we can make a difference!

title: Event Organization Guide
text:
Shun Hing College Event Organization Guidelines
Your ultimate guide to initiating something in the college
For an event scheduled in academic year 26-27 (September 2026 to May 2027), submit your proposal before 1 March 2027.
*****
We encourage every college student to initiate something here and contribute to our community.
Please read the full guide carefully and follow it strictly
when you organize events in Shun Hing College to help us keep things organized and maximize efficiency. (Updated on 6 September 2026)
*Note: This guide is for organizing events that use college resources (e.g., long-time occupation of public space, budget, branding, staff, etc.) only.
1. Planning (Application & Event-coverage, Poster Design)
Plan your event by specifying the date, location, purpose, and format. Ensure you have at least 12 potential participants.
Find a tutor to support the event.
Submit a brief
proposal
(including purpose, date, budget, promotional materials, and a simple rundown), a list of potential participants, and an event poster to your supporting tutor
at least 10 working days before the proposed event date
. Final approval will be made by the College Master.
Wait for the approval of your event. (
Contact person: your supporting tutor
)
2. Preparing (Venue, Snacks, Equipment, Registration, Event Promotion & Mass email)
Book the venue
on the
college event calendars
through your supporting
tutor
.
Purchase materials or snacks for your event by cash and obtain an official receipt from the shop.
Consult your supporting tutor before making any purchases
.
Test the equipment
with your tutor
at least two days before the event (
equipment guideline:
A-303A AV system
;
4/F Lobby AV system
). You should NOT operate the AV system on your own without prior approval from your event tutor. The AV system might only be available for events that are officially listed on the college calendar or requested during designated periods.
Apply for event coverage and draft your event social media post. Please contact
Media Team
with your brief run-down, image requirements, and the person responsible for writing event captions
at least 5 working days in advance
. After editing, the photos will be available in college
Flickr albums
, college
Facebook
, and
Instagram
. If the college
Media Team
is unavailable, please select the 10 best photos (landscape or portrait orientation, minimum dimensions of 3000 x 2000 pixels, no filters applied) and send them via a single cloud drive service, such as Google Drive, to
Media Team
within 24 hours after your event
. WhatsApp compressed images are not acceptable.
Ask your supporting tutor to assist with sending out the
mass email
using the
college’s mass email template
and printing the poster (
For an internal event, 2 working days in advance; for a JCSV III event, 5 working days in advance
).
Residents are not allowed to request a mass email without approval from a Tutorial Team member.
If you intend to apply for reimbursement, you must create a registration form through your mass emails and posters to collect participants’ names, UIDs, and room numbers. An official attendance record based on this registration is required by the Village III General Office.
3. Event Day
Prepare a separate participant list
for those from outside the college or village and provide it to security (through your tutor) to grant them access.
Arrive early
to ensure the venue is ready.
Maintain
an attendance record
with participants' names, university numbers, and room numbers.
Close the curtains after 19:00, and avoid playing loud music after 22:30 to
prevent disturbing neighbors
.
Clean up the venue after the event and dispose of
all trash in the bins outside the 4th-floor entrance.
4. After Event (Social Media Publishing, Reimbursement)
Within 24 hours after the event
, send the event caption (post draft for college social media) to
Media Team
, and send selected photos not taken by the
Media Team
. You can find reference posts from
college Facebook posts
. All social media posts will be published within 3 days after the event. This includes posts on
Facebook
and
Instagram
, videos on
YouTube
, as well as the original-size photos on
Flickr
.
Your event supporting tutor must review and verify your reimbursement claims files before submission. You must include your supporting
tutor
in all communication emails with the Village General Office.
All reimbursement claims must be submitted to the SoConnect Online Claim System by supporting tutor strictly within 14 days.
Gather feedback from participants to improve your event for next time.

title: Shun Hing Exchange Scholarships 25-26
text:
Shun Hing Exchange Scholarships 2025-26
The
Shun Hing College Exchange Scholarship
is awarded to second or third-year undergraduate students who will be partaking in academic exchange for a year to universities in Japan under the HKU Worldwide Exchange Scheme or faculty-level exchange programmes.
Ma Cheuk Yin
-Exchange at University of Tokyo -
My name is Jiwoong Choi, a humble Korean student in the Bachelor of Arts program at the University of Hong Kong. Currently I’m spending my 3
rd
year as an exchange student at the University of Tokyo. Before I explain a bit more about my life in Japan, I would first like to express my deepest gratitude for having received the Shun Hing Scholarships for my exchange program. It’ll be of great help in pursuing countless opportunities during my time in Japan.
As an Arts student, my major is French but I also have an additional minor in the Japanese language. One of the most important factors in acquiring a language is how real of an experience can you gain during the process. To fully embrace a language, you must first understand the culture of the people that use it. The best way to do so is obviously living amongst them for a good amount of time, which is exactly what my exchange program in UTokyo is granting me of.
I’m looking forward to what I’ll come across during my stay in one of the grandest metropolises in the world, and I’ve no doubt that it’s going to be an enriching experience that I would treasure for a lifetime.
Lau Pak Kiu Ambrose
- Exchange at Rikkyo University-
I am a third-year BSc student majoring in Environmental Science and Japanese Studies at the University of Hong Kong. I am studying at Rikkyo University in the College of Intercultural Communication for the 2025-26 academic year. I am grateful for the opportunity to spend my year studying abroad in Japan, as I have always been fascinated by all aspects of the country, especially its history and culture.
My time in Japan will be a significant boost in my goal of mastering the Japanese language. Living in Japan allows me to fully immerse myself in the language, whether in daily life or while socializing with fellow classmates. Admittedly, I have never been good at socializing, and I rarely participate in university events. However, I plan to join more extracurricular activities at Rikkyo, as this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to experience authentic foreign culture. Academically, in addition to Rikkyo’s excellent Japanese language program, I plan to take Japanese-taught courses and challenge myself in the spring semester.
I will make the most of my time here and explore as much of Japan as possible. I look forward to my ventures in Japan in the coming months, exploring all that this enchanting country has to offer. I will make the most of this opportunity and create memories that will last a lifetime.
Finally, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the HKU Japanese Studies Department and the Shun Hing College for this wonderful opportunity.
Yuka Yamane
- Exchange at Waseda University-
I am a third-year student majoring in Psychology and minoring in General Linguistics at the University of Hong Kong. I am incredibly grateful to have been awarded the Shun Hing Exchange Scholarship, which will greatly enrich my year at Waseda University and my experience in Japan.
This scholarship offers me an incredible opportunity to explore a variety of unique courses in Japanese linguistics and language that aren’t available at HKU. It enables me to delve deeper into my passion for linguistics, as well as my enthusiasm for Japanese culture and language. The prospect of learning directly about the connections between linguistic theory and the Japanese language, along with the relationships and distinctions between Japanese and English, is truly exciting.
As someone who is half-Japanese, I am eager to live in Japan and connect with my roots, while also simultaneously enhancing my Japanese language skills by immersing myself in the culture and talking with locals. Additionally, I plan to travel to other prefectures with new friends, exploring the country’s rich nature, food, and traditions.
Once again, I want to express my heartfelt gratitude for this scholarship, as it will enable me to have an unforgettable exchange experience, both academically and socially.

text:
Shun Hing Exchange Scholarships 2024-25
The
Shun Hing College Exchange Scholarship
is awarded to second or third-year undergraduate students who will be partaking in academic exchange for a year to universities in Japan under the HKU Worldwide Exchange Scheme or faculty-level exchange programmes.
Ma Cheuk Yin
-Exchange at University of Tokyo -
I am not the type of guy who always participates in various events or makes good use of different opportunities offered by my university. However, the Japanese Studies Department encourages its students to participate in an exchange programme to visit Japan. Together with my strong interest in Japanese history and culture, I applied for the exchange programme, which turned out to be one of the best decisions I have ever made.
Since the University of Tokyo offers diverse history and Japanese culture courses that align with my interests and current studies, I chose it as the institution where I will spend my time during my third year of undergraduate study. I have taken courses in disparate topics, from Japanese education to American religious history, which are rarely seen at HKU. This is a great opportunity for me to further explore my interests and review my desired career path.
Apart from studying, I will also visit different museums, temples, and shrines during the holidays. Thanks to the scholarship, I can visit and explore more of Japan since travelling across Japan is quite expensive, and it helps a lot with my financial pressures.
Siu Yin Ping
- Exchange at University of Tokyo-
I am currently a third-year student at the University of Hong Kong, pursuing a double major in General Linguistics and Japanese Studies. I am deeply honored to have received the Shun Hing Exchange Scholarship, which has enabled me to embark on a full-year exchange program at the University of Tokyo. This opportunity allows me to engage in courses related to language acquisition and Japanese language teaching — two areas I am passionate about. Through this program, I am able to learn first-hand how linguistic theory and Japanese pedagogy intersect, expanding my understanding of language from both structural and cultural perspectives.
Living in Japan has been a transformative experience, enriching my life in countless ways. It has sharpened my Japanese language skills and provided a nuanced insight into Japanese culture, history, and society. This immersive environment has also broadened my worldview, allowing me to appreciate the complexities of cross-cultural communication and connection. I am committed to making the most of this academic year by fully engaging with my studies and embracing every opportunity to build lasting connections.
Sun Shengyao
- Exchange at University of Tokyo-
I am a third-year Engineering student majoring in Computer Engineering and I'm currently participating in an exchange program at the University of Tokyo, one of the world’s top universities for engineering. This is a remarkable opportunity for me to expand my knowledge and skills, and I am eager to learn and experience as much as possible during my time here.
My passion for Japanese culture began at a young age, primarily through anime and games, which helped me develop my language skills. I achieved the JLPT N1 certification before my departure, enabling me to take all my major courses in Japanese alongside local students. I have enrolled in courses such as Very-Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) Design, Operating Systems, Distributed Systems, Quantum Computing, and other fundamental topics in my field. I aim to integrate the knowledge I’ve acquired from both HKU and UTokyo, gaining a comprehensive understanding of computer architecture to make meaningful contributions to the world in the future.
I am excited about the coming months and look forward to exploring Japan, engaging with locals, and immersing myself in Japanese culture. I am confident that this experience will enrich my personal and academic growth, shaping me into a more well-rounded individual upon my return to Hong Kong.
Finally, I would like to express my sincere gratitude for being awarded this scholarship. It will undoubtedly be a great support for my time and experiences in Japan.

title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club and The University of Hong Kong
text:
The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust has donated an average of HK$1.6 billion to the community every year over the past decade by way of its own major initiatives and donations, supporting projects of well over 100 charitable groups and organisations each year. These encompass ten major areas; namely, Arts, Culture & Heritage, Education & Training, Elderly Services, Emergency & Poverty Relief, Environmental Protection, Family Services, Medical & Health, Rehabilitation Services, Sports & Recreation, and Youth Development.
In 2013/14, the total approved charitable donations were over HK$3.6 billion, an increase of 85% on the previous year. The approved donations benefited 168 charities and community projects.
For over half a century, The University of Hong Kong’s close partnership with the Trust has enhanced its ability to strive for excellence in education, scholarship, and research. The Hong Kong Jockey Club has sponsored over 80 academic-related projects at the University, totalling some HK$1.6 billion.
Student Village
The Trust recognises the importance of the residential experience, and its support of residential education at the University includes the construction of the Jockey Club Student Villages I, II and III, which opened in 2002, 2006 and 2015 respectively. Residential Halls and Colleges in these three Villages provide accommodation for over 3,600 students.

The College Hall at the Village, designed by Index Architecture Limited, was awarded the “Honor Award for Interiors Architecture” by the 2014 American Institute of Architects (HK Chapter) Honors & Awards Program. The grand piano was a gift from Dr Serena Yang.

地圖搜尋
(使用Google地圖搜尋 「22.279180, 114.128797」 或 「9 Lung Wah Street」)
1
由香港國際機場前往
乘坐機場快綫
Ø   乘坐機場快綫往（中環）香港站，車費為港幣 115 元，車程大約 24 分鐘。
Ø   然後於香港站乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 20 分鐘）。
Ø   亦可步行至中環站轉乘港島綫往堅尼地城站，於 A 出口離開車站後依照地圖紫色箭咀所示步行 15 分鐘，或乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
乘坐巴士
Ø   步出接機大堂後經右邊緩坡道前往巴士站乘坐巴士路線
A10
往堅尼地城或
A11
往上環。
Ø   如果乘坐路線
A10
，於「北街」（車站 10）或「聯邦新樓」（車站 11）下車。然後依照地圖紫色箭咀所示步行 15 分鐘，或乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
Ø   如果乘坐路線
A11
，於「港澳碼頭」（車站 5）下車。然後於港澳碼頭的士站乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 15 分鐘）。
2
由港珠澳大橋前往
乘坐巴士
Ø   於港珠澳大橋香港口岸乘坐巴士路線 A10 往堅尼地城或 A11 往上環。
Ø   如果乘坐路線
A10
，於「北街」（車站 10）或「聯邦新樓」（車站 11）下車。然後依照地圖紫色箭咀所示步行 15 分鐘，或乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
Ø   如果乘坐路線
A11
，於「港澳碼頭」（車站 5）下車。然後於港澳碼頭的士站乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 15 分鐘）。
3
由高鐵香港西九龍站前往
乘坐港鐵
Ø   從香港西九龍站B2層抵港大堂經A出口步行至柯士甸站。
Ø   乘坐港鐵屯馬綫至紅磡站並轉乘東鐵綫往金鐘站，然後轉乘港島綫往堅尼地城站。
Ø   於 A 出口離開車站後依照地圖紫色箭咀所示步行 15 分鐘，或乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
乘坐巴士
Ø   如果你只攜帶輕便行李，可於西區海底隧道巴士轉乘站乘坐路線
971
，於「北街」（車站21）或「聯邦新樓」（車站 22）下車。然後根據地圖上顯示的紫色箭咀步行15分鐘，或乘坐計程車前往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
4
由羅湖或落馬洲（東鐵線）前往
Ø   乘坐港鐵東鐵綫至金鐘站並轉乘港島綫往堅尼地城站。
Ø   於 A 出口離開車站後依照地圖紫色箭咀所示步行 15 分鐘，或乘坐的士往學生村（車程大約 5 分鐘）。
5
由任何地點乘坐的士前往
請確保的士司機按計程錶收費。如攜帶行李或行車路線經過收費隧道或路段，乘客須額外繳付相關附加費。請瀏覽香港特別行政區政府運輸署網址
https://www.td.gov.hk/en/transport_in_hong_kong/public_transport/taxi/taxi_fare_of_hong_kong/index.html
參閱更多相關資料
如的士司機不確定行車路線，你可以向其展示以下訊息：
請你載我到龍華街9號「香港大學賽馬會第三學生村」（位於堅尼地城觀龍樓前面）。請沿干諾道西向西行到城西道，沿城西道進入山市街。靠右行駛，直行到第二個交通燈位轉右進入卑路乍街，再在第二個路口轉左進入士美菲路。沿途直上，經過石山街、科士街和蒲飛路路口，在電訊盈科堅尼地城電話機房後的第一個路口轉右進入龍華街往觀龍樓方向行駛，中途左手邊的大玻璃門便是香港大學賽馬會第三學生村正門。
其他資訊
非本地新生建議在抵港時購買八達通卡。
當乘坐的士往學生村時，請確保司機按照計程錶收費，並向司機索取機印收據。如果有攜帶個人行李或行車路線經過收費隧道、收費道路或收費區，須另付規定的附加費用。請參閱運輸署網頁https://www.td.gov.hk/tc/transport_in_hong_kong/public_transport/taxi/index.html。
雖然有綠色小巴從堅尼地城開往學生村，但是司機可能不允許攜帶大件行李登車而不建議乘坐。

6.1.   If  you  have  changed  other  settings  on  the  audio  mixer,  please  ask  your  tutor  to  use  the  CUELIST  function  to  
recover
 
the
 
settings.
 6.2.   To  turn  off  the  mixer  on  the  right  side,  hold  the  power  button  (in  the  upper  right  corner)  for  three  seconds.  After  it  
starts
 
to
 
blink,
 
click
 
once.
 6.3.  Turn  off  the  wireless  mics  6.4.  Turn  off  the  main  power  of  the  audio  system  6.5.  Turn  off  the  projector  by  red  button  the  panel  on  the  wall.  6.6.  You  don’t  need  to  turn  off  the  speakers  and  their  power.  6.7.  Fully  close  the  curtain  of  the  projector  screen  and  mirror.

text:
Tutorial Team
We are here for your ideal college experience
Prof. David S. Lee
College Master
BFin(AMPB) Deputy Programme Director
BFin(AMPB) Admissions Tutor
Associate Professor of Teaching
HKU Business School
Email:
dslee@hku.hk
Prof. David S. Lee
is an award-winning teacher that is active broadly in the areas of ethics, fintech, leadership, law, and corporate governance. A recipient of multiple teaching awards, David is the first business academic to ever receive a
UGC Teaching Award
, the highest university teaching honor in Hong Kong. David feels teaching is a wonderful privilege and enjoys being in the classroom and engaging with students.
Combining his interests in ethics, finance, technology, and teaching, David is a co-instructor for a first of its kind massive open online course (MOOC) titled,
FinTech Ethics and Risks
. David is also co-author of the first Asia focused business ethics textbook,
Business Ethics: Ethical Decision Making and Cases, An Asia Edition
(Cengage Learning Asia, 2019). His commentary and writing regularly appear in print and broadcast media and have been featured in the
Harvard Business Review, Arirang TV, Handelsblatt, the Nikkei Asian Review, The Korea Times, and the South China Morning Post
.
Prior to joining the University of Hong Kong, David worked in investment management. He started his career at Goldman Sachs and also has experience as a lawyer, in management consulting, and working with entrepreneurial ventures.
David received his legal education from UCLA, graduate degrees from the LSE and Harvard, post-graduate training at Cambridge, and his undergraduate education from Brigham Young University.
Previously, David served as the inaugural Director for career development at
HKU Business School
and is especially interested in helping students as they consider and prepare for different career and life paths.
David and his family are excited to be part of the Shun Hing College community.
